title: Legacy Shared-UID Split Segments (RECURRENCE-ID with RRULE/RDATE): Read-Only Expansion

citations.verbatim_quote: If present, this JSCalendar object represents one occurrence of a recurring JSCalendar object. If present, the "recurrenceRules" and "recurrenceOverrides" properties MUST NOT be present.

A VEVENT (or VTODO) component is a recurrence override if it has the RECURRENCE-ID property set, and the iCalendar object contains a VEVENT (or VTODO) component that does not have the RECURRENCE-ID but the RRULE property set, and the UID property values of the two components are equal. The component without the RECURRENCE-ID property is in that case referred to as the "main component".

Assuming an unbounded recurring calendar component scheduled to occur on Mondays and Wednesdays, the "RANGE" parameter could not be used to reschedule only the future Monday instances to occur on Tuesday instead. In such cases, the calendar application could simply truncate the unbounded recurring calendar component (i.e., with the "COUNT" or "UNTIL" rule parts), and create two new unbounded recurring calendar components for the future instances.

rationale: Per RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1, draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 2.1.2, and invariant I-C-006, a conformant calendar store MUST NEVER emit a component carrying both `RECURRENCE-ID` and `RRULE`/`RDATE` on any write operation—splits MUST create a new-UID component per RFC 8984 Section 4.1.3 (R-L3-001). However, existing persisted calendars created by older stores may contain legacy shared-UID split segments (a component sharing the original `UID` with `RECURRENCE-ID` set to the split occurrence and `RRULE` set to the future schedule alongside a truncated master component). To avoid losing user events when reading such persisted calendars, read-only timeline expansion treats each recurring component (`RRULE` or `RDATE` present) as an independent recurring segment while applying standalone overrides (`RECURRENCE-ID` present and neither `RRULE` nor `RDATE` present) on top. How a store migrates or mutates such legacy shared-UID segments upon subsequent `edit` or `delete` operations is intentionally left as an open migration policy question (and rejected on write by the reference oracle).
store_implication:
1. Write prohibition: No store write operation (`add`, `edit`, `delete`) may ever create a component that carries both `RECURRENCE-ID` and `RRULE`/`RDATE`/`EXDATE` (enforced by invariant I-C-006).
2. Legacy read-only expansion: When reading an imported or pre-existing persisted calendar containing a legacy shared-UID split segment (`legacy_input: true` in specification scenarios), timeline expansion MUST expand every component carrying `RRULE` or `RDATE` as a recurring segment (applying its own `EXDATE` exclusions) and apply standalone overrides (`RECURRENCE-ID` with neither `RRULE` nor `RDATE`) by matching occurrence `RECURRENCE-ID`.
3. Open question on write: Modifying (`edit` or `delete`) a `UID` that currently holds legacy shared-UID split segments is unspecified by this specification (requiring an explicit store migration policy, such as upgrading legacy segments to distinct UIDs on write); the reference oracle raises `StoreError` when a write targets such a `UID`.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Reading a persisted calendar with `[segment2(uid=U, rid=20250503T090000, rrule=FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=2), master(uid=U, rid=None, rrule=FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=20250503T085959)]`: read-only expansion emits all 4 occurrences (May 1..2 from master and May 3..4 from segment2) rather than dropping segment2's RRULE.
Attempting to add or produce a component with both `recurrence_id` and `rrule` during a normal store write violates invariant I-C-006 and MUST be rejected.

scenarios.name: expand_legacy_shared_uid_split_calendar_reads_all_segments
scenarios.description: Read-only timeline expansion of a pre-existing calendar containing a legacy shared-UID split segment (RECURRENCE-ID plus RRULE) alongside a truncated master emits occurrences from both segments.

audit_notes: Added R-L3-009 to isolate legacy shared-UID split calendars strictly as read-only backward-compatible inputs (`legacy_input: true`), never valid store write outputs (enforced by I-C-006).
Verified all citations against rfc8984.txt, draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar.txt, and rfc5545.txt.
